SIGNATURE — The busiest Ilha Grande crossing: Conceição de Jacareí is the closest mainland pier to car-free Abraão, 15–20 min by flexboat, fares R$45–150 one-way depending on season/operator (typical R$60), embarkation tax R$10.30/leg. Haversine 6.5 nm + 0.5 nm threading the channel islets.

The Lopes Mendes shuttle: taxi boats run Abraão–Pouso all day so visitors can walk the 20-min trail to Brazil's most-awarded beach (mapped as an OSM boat route). Haversine 1.9 nm + 0.6 nm wrapping the Ponta do Pouso headlands.
Mainland coastal link between the two Ilha Grande gateways — today a 30-min drive on the BR-101. Haversine 7.8 nm + 0.5 nm coastal wrap along the Mangaratiba shore.

Cross-market Costa Verde heritage corridor: Angra to Paraty's colonial quay along the mainland shore. Haversine 25.2 nm + ~2.8 nm coastal wrap; 28 nm kept consistent with the Paraty package (paraty-brazil/route-inventory.json holds the mirror record to bp-dbf5302ce6).

The beach express up the Baía do Guajará: weekend Geladão Fluvial today (220-pax lancha, ~1h40 via Icoaraci, R$20). Destination BP coordinate is null; distance estimated from the candidate Mosqueiro pier (haversine 16.6 nm) + wrap margin north along Mosqueiro's west coast to the Vila trapiche — RE-COMPUTE once the Tavernard trapiche coordinate is confirmed. Genuinely iconic locally; held at non-signature pending coordinate confirmation.

One of Pará's busiest regulated lines: Arapari's hourly ~62-pax lanchas, 45–60 min tide-dependent, R$17.58–18. Origin BP coordinate null (new terminal); distance computed from the Cidade Velha waterfront candidate pier: haversine 7.5 nm + ~3.5 nm coastal-wrap margin because the direct line crosses Ilha das Onças — the navigable path wraps south of the island via the furos. RE-COMPUTE on coordinate confirmation.

Heritage-port bay corridor: Paranaguá's Rua da Praia waterfront to the island, 1h30 by lancha today (~R$80-90). Haversine 10.9 nm + ~1 nm coastal-wrap margin for the buoyed channel around Ilha da Cotinga. Signature corridor #2.
Paranaguá to the southern village — Abaline runs a 07:30 Paranaguá→Encantadas departure. Haversine 10.6 nm + channel-wrap margin.

Daily nautical-taxi link (~50 min) to the isolated municipal seat of Guaraqueçaba — water is the practical access, the road is a poor dirt track. Haversine 16.5 nm + ~2.5 nm wrap for the winding northern-bay channels between islands.

Tarumã leisure spur from the Ponta Negra hotel zone up into the Tarumã-Açu inlet's private-marina cluster — rounds out the Rio Negro recreational mesh and a charging-host candidate. Haversine 2.0 nm plus inlet-entry margin.

SIGNATURE — The UNESCO twin-site crossing: Paraty's colonial quay to car-free Vila do Abraão. Real transfer corridor today (shared boat from R$330 pp, private lancha from R$1,890, ~1.5 h). Haversine 30.4 nm + ~0.6 nm margin threading the bay's island field. Cross-market route; the Angra market holds the Abraão-side node (rn- route family).

failed.description: Costa Verde heritage corridor: Paraty to Angra dos Reis along the mainland shore of the Baía da Ilha Grande. Haversine 25.2 nm + ~2.8 nm coastal wrap; kept at ~28 nm for consistency with the Angra market brief (Angra ↔ Paraty ~28 nm). No scheduled service today — the corridor is driven by road.

Inter-market line-haul: Paraty to Ilhabela's Pier da Vila. Haversine 48.9 nm + ~3 nm wrap around the Ponta da Juatinga; held at 52 nm to match the existing Ilhabela inventory entry (ssb-ilb-pier-da-vila ↔ paraty-waterfront, 52 nm aspirational). Within the 70 nm electric envelope but a long open-coast leg — note near-range planning margin.

The lifeline to Ilha Diana, the fishing-village island in the estuary served today by the public boat from the Centro terminal. Coastal-wrap margin added: the navigable path follows the winding port channel north, not the straight line.
The existing small-boat link from Ponta da Praia to Santa Cruz dos Navegantes on the Guarujá shore (the OSM-mapped 'Santos–Praia do Góes e N.S. dos Navegantes' service), landing by Marina Dolfin.
Cross-channel connector between the cruise terminal and Vicente de Carvalho — the same axis the 2031 road tunnel will serve for vehicles, available on the water today.
Ponta da Praia to Porto Marina Astúrias — a direct marina spur linking the Santos leisure waterfront to Guarujá's main marina without the balsa queue.
Ponta da Praia to Ilha das Palmas, the private club island in Santos Bay (Clube de Pesca de Santos, founded 1934) — a classic members-and-events shuttle, boat-only by definition.
Guarujá balsa head south to Porto Marina Astúrias along the Guarujá shore — the marina feeder for the crossing.
Marina Astúrias to boat-only Praia do Góes — a two-minute beach hop around the Santa Cruz dos Navegantes point; small wrap margin for the headland.

The Canal de Bertioga run: from Ponta da Praia up the port channel and east through the mangrove-lined canal behind Santo Amaro island to the Bertioga crossing. Generous coastal-wrap margin — the navigable path winds through the estuary and canal, far off the straight line.
Santa Cruz dos Navegantes to Praia do Góes — the short hop between the fishing community's marina and its boat-only beach neighbour.

The state ferry corridor across the Baía de São Marcos (1.8M pax record year; 71.7k pax in 11 Carnival days). Foot-passenger foiling express alongside the vehicle ferry. Direct bay crossing; haversine distance.
Historic-center to the Baixada road-head at Cujupe — a foot-passenger link that skips the drive out to Ponta da Espera. Direct bay path; haversine distance.

Alcântara local link: town pier to the Cujupe road-head, connecting the colonial center to the Baixada bus/vehicle gateway. Haversine 8.3 nm plus ~0.7 nm coastal-wrap margin along the Alcântara shore and its off-lying banks.
Hotel-district departure to the Baixada road-head — the second leg of a tide-independent network out of Ponta d'Areia. Direct bay path; haversine distance.

The Lençóis Maranhenses gateway leg from the state's own project pipeline (São Luís–Icatu ferry to shorten the Barreirinhas run). Distance measured to Icatu town waterfront reference (-2.7752,-44.0644, Nominatim town center — pier site unconfirmed, BP coords null): haversine 12.6 nm plus ~1.4 nm margin for the Baía de São José shoals; treat as indicative until a terminal site is fixed.

Costa Verde link: Ilhabela's historic village to Paraty's UNESCO colonial harbour. 48.8 nm direct; routed around Ponta das Canas with sea-room margin ⇒ ~52 nm — inside the 70 nm electric envelope with reserve; shore charging needed at the Paraty end. Cross-market corridor to the Angra dos Reis–Paraty network.
